main_text.p: qui illud divino suo dirigit nutu. Ideo ante Cæsaream suam Majestatem, tabula eadem inscriptione dependet, & pro verbo Cor depictum est ♡, laurea coronatum, significans, Cor Cæsareæ Majestatis cunctis virtutibus & honoribus ornatum & coronatum esse.

Et quia verissimè constat, Majestatem quondam Cæsaream claritate sua & ornatu illud idem fuisse in terris, quod splendor Solis in cœlis: ideo supra illam scriptum est: Quod in cœlis Sol, hoc in terra Cæsar. Pro verbo vero Solis, depictus est ⊙, & pro verbo Cæsar, Aquila.
Et quoniam Moderatio & Providentia Rationi sunt conjunctæ, ideo equi duo, Rationi propinqui, duabus illis dirigiuntur virtutibus, ut Currus moderatè & omni gubernetur providentia.
Sequentes duo equi per Alacritatem & Opportunitatem dirigiuntur: quia quemadmodum opportunè Currum incedere decet, ita id alacriter fieri oportet.

page.notes: Printed line-end extension marks after "Majestatem", "Majestatis", "quia" and "fuisse" are typesetting devices, not notes. The word "omnt" in the third paragraph is printed that way; the letter before "t" may be an i with a superscript, so it is likely "omni" but I copied the printed form as read. Italic and roman boundaries in the mixed passages are approximate. The page number 167 is read from the head; the final figure is clear. The catchword "equos" and signature "L 4" are at the foot.
